mainTopic: Betrothing with a debt: the disputes over a שטר חוב and a spoken loan, and failed attempts to show that מקדש במלוה is a dispute between תנאים
overview: This amud explains the argument between רבי מאיר and חכמים about making קידושין with a debt. For a שטר חוב owed by someone else, the גמרא gives two explanations. Either they argue about שמואל's rule that the seller can still cancel the debt, or everyone accepts שמואל and they argue only about whether the woman trusts the note. For a spoken loan, the argument depends on whether רב's rule of מעמד שלשתן covers a loan or only a פקדון. Next the גמרא tries to show that betrothing with a loan she owes him (מקדש במלוה) is itself a dispute between תנאים, using a ברייתא about betrothing with a שטר. That proof is pushed off three ways: the שטר had no witnesses, it was written שלא לשמה (following ריש לקיש), or it was written for her but without her knowledge. A second try uses a ברייתא about a craftsman who makes jewelry for a woman. The גמרא rejects this too. Everyone may agree a loan cannot betroth, and the real argument is whether a wage is owed from the beginning of the work to the end. Each side's view is explained on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל's rule: a sold debt can still be cancelled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting שמואל: if someone sells a שטר חוב and then cancels the debt, it is cancelled, and even his heir can cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone sells a debt document to another person and then goes back and cancels the debt, it is cancelled. Even his heir can cancel it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting שמואל's rule so it can use that rule to explain the argument about using a שטר חוב for קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling a שטר חוב does not fully cut the original lender off from the debt. He can still cancel it, and so can his heir. This means the buyer, or a woman who receives the note, could end up holding a worthless piece of paper.

keyTerms.meaning: A written document recording a debt

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the danger at the center of the whole argument. Whoever received the note can lose its value at any moment.

phrases.english: One who sells a promissory note to his fellow,
and then went back and forgave it, it is forgiven,
and even an heir can forgive it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמּוֹכֵר שְׁטַר חוֹב לַחֲבֵירוֹ, וְחָזַר וּמְחָלוֹ – מָחוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quote of שמואל that the גמרא introduced just before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seller of a שטר חוב, or his heir, can still cancel the debt, and the cancellation works.

steps.title: First explanation: one side follows שמואל and one side does not
steps.stepSummary: The argument about a שטר חוב depends on שמואל. חכמים agree with שמואל, and רבי מאיר does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds like שמואל, and the other Sage does not hold like שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses שמואל's rule to explain why the two sides disagree about making קידושין with a שטר חוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים agree with שמואל, so the man could still cancel the debt. The woman therefore does not trust the note, and she is not מקודשת. רבי מאיר disagrees with שמואל, so the note is secure, the woman trusts it, and she is מקודשת.

keyTerms.meaning: One Sage (a polite way to say 'this one' or 'that one')
He does not hold (does not agree with)

steps.confusionAlert: The text only says 'מר' (one Sage) and 'מר' (the other Sage). From the context, the first is חכמים and the second is רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: For one Sage holds like שמואל,
phrases.notes: This is חכמים: since the debt can be cancelled, she doesn't trust the note.

phrases.english: and the other Sage does not hold like שמואל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies שמואל's rule to the argument about קידושין
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument about a שטר חוב comes down to whether one accepts שמואל's rule.

steps.title: Second explanation: everyone agrees with שמואל, and they argue about the woman's trust
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, everyone accepts שמואל. They argue only about whether a woman relies on the note anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you could say that everyone agrees with שמואל. Here they argue about a woman. One Sage holds that a woman does trust the note, because she says to herself: 'He would not ignore me and cancel the debt for others.' The other Sage holds that even a woman does not trust it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different way to explain the same argument, one where nobody rejects שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the disagreement is about how the woman thinks, not about the law of cancelling debts. רבי מאיר says she feels confident the man won't cancel the debt and hurt her, so she relies on the note. חכמים say even a woman doesn't trust it enough, since he could still cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another explanation)
She relies on it (she feels secure)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain the argument about a שטר חוב. Either they argue about שמואל's law, or everyone accepts שמואל and they argue about whether the woman trusts the note.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
everyone holds like שמואל,
and here they disagree about a woman.
One Sage holds: a woman relies on it,
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר, which is why he says she is מקודשת.

phrases.english: since she says to herself:
he would not leave me aside
and forgive the debt for others,
and the other Sage holds:
even a woman does not rely on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation of the argument in place of the first
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both sides accept שמואל. They argue about whether a woman trusts a cancellable note.

steps.title: What about a spoken loan?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the two sides argue about when the man uses a loan with no document.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a spoken loan, what do they argue about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the second case, a loan made by word of mouth, and asks what the argument is based on. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule was about a written note. A loan with no document needs a different explanation, so the גמרא opens a new question.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan made by word of mouth, with no document

phrases.english: With a loan by word of mouth,
what do they disagree about?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the written-debt case to the spoken-loan case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the basis of the argument when the קידושין uses a spoken loan?

steps.title: רב's rule of מעמד שלשתן
steps.stepSummary: The argument depends on רב's rule. If all three people are present, a person can transfer money that someone else is holding for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue about רב הונא's statement in the name of רב. For רב הונא said in the name of רב: if someone says, 'I have a מנה in your hands, give it to so-and-so,' and all three of them are present, the third person acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing רב's rule about transferring money when all three people stand together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, transferring something requires a formal act of acquiring it. רב teaches that when the owner, the holder, and the receiver are all present, simply saying the words is enough. The next step shows how the two sides read this rule differently.

keyTerms.meaning: When all three of them are present

phrases.english: About the statement of רב הונא in the name of רב,
for רב הונא said in the name of רב:
'I have a hundred in your hand,'
'give it to so-and-so,'
if all three are present, he has acquired it.
phrases.notes: The three are the owner, the one holding the money, and the person receiving it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 by bringing רב's rule
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument is about רב's rule of מעמד שלשתן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When all three people are present, money held by another person can be transferred by speech alone.

steps.title: Does רב's rule apply to a loan or only to a deposit?
steps.stepSummary: חכמים limit רב's rule to a פקדון. רבי מאיר applies it to a loan too.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds: when רב said this, he meant only a deposit, not a loan. The other Sage holds: there is no difference between a loan and a deposit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how each side reads רב's rule. That reading decides whether a spoken loan can be used for קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פקדון is real money still sitting with the holder. A loan has already been spent, so only a debt remains. חכמים say רב's rule works only for a פקדון, so the woman receives nothing and is not מקודשת. רבי מאיר says it works for a loan too, so she is מקודשת.

keyTerms.meaning: A deposit (an item or money held for someone, still intact)
A loan (money given to be spent and paid back later)

steps.whatToRemember: For a spoken loan, the argument is whether רב's rule of מעמד שלשתן covers a loan (רבי מאיר) or only a פקדון (חכמים).

phrases.english: One Sage holds:
phrases.notes: This is חכמים, who say the woman is not מקודשת.

phrases.english: when רב said it,
that applies to a deposit,
but a loan, no.
And the other Sage holds:
no difference whether a loan
or a deposit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: כִּי קָאָמַר רַב הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּפִקָּדוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how each side reads רב's rule from step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חכמים limit מעמד שלשתן to a פקדון. רבי מאיר applies it to a loan as well.

steps.title: A ברייתא about betrothing with a document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the question of betrothing with a loan is a dispute between תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא with three opinions about a man who betroths a woman with a שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is a dispute between תנאים. If a man says, 'Be betrothed to me with a document': רבי מאיר says she is not betrothed. רבי אלעזר says she is betrothed. חכמים say we check the value of the paper. If it is worth a פרוטה, she is betrothed. If not, she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that it thinks might show תנאים arguing about betrothing with a loan. This step quotes the source; the next step explains why it might be about a loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three opinions. רבי מאיר says the betrothal does not work, רבי אלעזר says it does, and חכמים take a middle path that depends only on what the paper is worth. Right now we do not yet know what kind of שטר this is. The next step tries to figure that out.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it is like a dispute between תנאים
Worth a פרוטה, the smallest amount of money that counts for קידושין

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute of תנאים:
"Be betrothed to me with a document"
Rabbi Meir says: she is not betrothed;
and Rabbi Elazar says: she is betrothed;
and the Sages say: we appraise the paper;

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה – מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת,
phrases.english: if it has the value of a peruta, she is betrothed;
and if not, she is not betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new attempt to tie the topic of מקדש במלוה to a dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That betrothing with a loan is a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about הִתְקַדְּשִׁי לִי בִּשְׁטָר with three opinions

steps.title: The document must be a note for her own debt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of שטר the ברייתא means. It cannot be a note for a debt that other people owe him, because רבי מאיר already said elsewhere that such a note works. So it must be a note for her own debt to him, and the argument is about betrothing with a loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of document is this? If you say it is a note for a debt others owe him, then רבי מאיר contradicts himself. So it must be a note for her own debt, and they are arguing about betrothing with a loan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא figures out which kind of שטר the ברייתא is talking about. It concludes that the תנאים are arguing about betrothing with a loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In an earlier ברייתא, רבי מאיר said a woman is betrothed with a note for a debt that others owe the man. So here, where רבי מאיר says she is not betrothed, the note cannot be that kind. It must be a note for money she herself owes him. That means the case is really betrothal with a loan she already has.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the details?
A written note that proves a debt
Betrothing a woman with a loan she owes him

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse two different notes. A note for a debt that others owe him is something new he gives her. A note for her own debt is just a loan she already has.

phrases.english: This document, what are its circumstances?
If we say it is a promissory note of a debt owed by others,
then Rabbi Meir contradicts Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: In an earlier ברייתא, רבי מאיר said she is betrothed with a note for a debt that others owe.

phrases.english: Rather, it is about a promissory note of her own debt,
and they disagree about one who betroths with a loan!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ברייתא from step 7 and shows why it would be about a loan.
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא's dispute is about מקדש במלוה
steps.raayaSupportSource: Ruling out a note owed by others, since that would make רבי מאיר contradict himself

steps.title: The case is a betrothal document with no witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects the proof. He says the ברייתא may be about a שטר קידושין with no witnesses signed on it, not a loan note at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: What case are we dealing with here? A case where he betrothed her with a document that has no witnesses on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק pushes back on the proof. He offers a different case for the ברייתא, so it does not have to be about a loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the שטר being a debt note. רב נחמן בר יצחק says it is a different kind of document: a שטר קידושין, a document that itself makes the betrothal. The missing witnesses are what the argument is about, not a loan.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
With what are we dealing here?
For example, where he betrothed her with a document
phrases.notes: He means a document of קידושין that does the betrothing, not a note for a debt.

phrases.english: that has no witnesses on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 8's conclusion that the ברייתא is about a loan.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the ברייתא shows תנאים arguing about מקדש במלוה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The שטר may be a שטר קידושין without witnesses, not a debt note

steps.title: Each opinion follows its own view about witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains the three opinions. רבי מאיר holds that the signing witnesses make a document work, so with no signatures it fails. רבי אלעזר holds that the witnesses to the handing-over make it work, so it succeeds. חכמים are unsure, so they count only the paper's value as money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר follows his own view that the signing witnesses make the document work. רבי אלעזר follows his own view that the witnesses to the handing-over make it work. חכמים are unsure whether the law follows רבי מאיר or רבי אלעזר. So they check the paper. If it is worth a פרוטה, she is betrothed. If not, she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק finishes his answer by showing how each opinion in the ברייתא fits his case. This ends the attempt to prove that תנאים argue about betrothing with a loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is really the well-known dispute about a גט: do the signing witnesses or the delivery witnesses make it work? חכמים are in doubt, so they do not rely on the document as a document. They treat the paper as a money gift, which works if it is worth a פרוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning that he holds elsewhere
Witnesses who watch the document being handed over
Make it work; literally 'cut', as a גט cuts the marriage

steps.whatToRemember: The proof fails. The ברייתא about a שטר may not be about loans at all. It can be read as the עדי חתימה versus עדי מסירה dispute, with חכמים in doubt and relying only on the paper's money value.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a case that looks like a dispute about loans can be explained through a completely different argument about witnesses.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir follows his reasoning, as he says:
signatory witnesses effect it;
phrases.notes: This comes from the laws of a גט. רבי מאיר holds the same for a שטר קידושין, so with no signatures it does nothing.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Elazar follows his reasoning, as he says:
witnesses to the transmission effect it;
and the Rabbis are uncertain

phrases.aramaic: אִי כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר אִי כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: whether it is like Rabbi Meir or like Rabbi Elazar;
therefore, we appraise the paper:
phrases.notes: Since they are unsure about the document, they treat the paper only as a money gift.

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה – מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת,
phrases.english: if it has the value of a peruta, she is betrothed;
and if not, she is not betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר לְטַעְמֵיהּ דְּאָמַר עֵדֵי חֲתִימָה כָּרְתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב נחמן בר יצחק's rejection by explaining each opinion in the ברייתא according to his case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: All three opinions fit the dispute between עדי חתימה and עדי מסירה, with no connection to loans

steps.title: Another explanation: the document was not written for her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a second way to read the ברייתא. The שטר was written שלא לשמה, and the תנאים argue about the view of ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, the case is one where he wrote the document not for her sake, and they argue about ריש לקיש's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another reason the ברייתא does not have to be about a loan. This line sets up ריש לקיש's question, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is still not about betrothing with a loan, so the proof from step 8 stays rejected. Now the problem with the שטר is not missing witnesses. It is that the שטר was not written for this specific woman.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: brings in another possible answer
Not for her sake: not written for this specific woman

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
for example, where he wrote it not for her sake,
phrases.notes: "It" is the שטר קידושין from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: and they disagree about the view of ריש לקיש.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, כְּגוֹן שֶׁכְּתָבוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a second, different way to push off the proof that steps 9-10 already rejected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It rejects reading the ברייתא as being about betrothing with a loan.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be explained as a שטר written שלא לשמה, so it has nothing to do with loans.

steps.title: ריש לקיש asks whether a betrothal document must be written for her
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks whether a שטר אירוסין written not for her sake works. Should betrothal be compared to divorce, or to the other ways of betrothing?
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש asked: what is the law of a betrothal document written not for her sake? Do we compare becoming married to leaving a marriage? A גט must be written for her, so a שטר אירוסין would have to be as well. Or do we compare the ways of becoming married to each other? Money does not have to be made for her, so a שטר would not have to be either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes ריש לקיש's question, which is the source for the disagreement just mentioned. He lays out two possible comparisons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one compares a שטר אירוסין to a גט, and a גט must be written לשמה. Side two compares a שטר to the coin used for קידושין, and nobody needs a coin made for a specific woman.

keyTerms.meaning: Becoming: becoming a man's wife through קידושין
Leaving: leaving a marriage through a גט
We compare (two things in the תורה, so the same rules apply)

phrases.english: For ריש לקיש asked:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁטַר אֵירוּסִין שֶׁכְּתָבוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: A betrothal document that he wrote not for her sake, what is the law?
Do we compare becoming married to leaving a marriage?
Just as for leaving, we require it to be for her sake,
so for becoming married too, we require it to be for her sake.
Or perhaps we compare the ways of becoming married to each other:

phrases.aramaic: מָה הֲוָיָה דְכֶסֶף לָא בָּעֵינַן לִשְׁמָהּ,
phrases.english: just as for becoming married with money, we do not require it to be for her sake,

phrases.aramaic: אַף הֲוָיָה דִשְׁטָר לָא בָּעֵינַן לִשְׁמָהּ.
phrases.english: so for becoming married with a document, we do not require it to be for her sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It gives the source of the ריש לקיש view that step 11 mentioned.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Must a שטר אירוסין be written לשמה like a גט, or is it like money, which needs no special purpose?

steps.title: ריש לקיש answers his own question from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers his own question. The פסוק puts leaving and becoming side by side, so a שטר אירוסין must be written לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he asked it, he answered it himself. The פסוק says "and she leaves... and becomes," so it compares becoming married to leaving a marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש settles his question. Becoming married is compared to leaving a marriage, so the betrothal document must be written for her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק joins the woman's leaving her first husband with her becoming another man's wife. That link makes the לשמה rule of a גט apply to a שטר אירוסין as well.

keyTerms.meaning: After he asked it, he went back and answered it

phrases.english: After he asked it, he went back and answered it:
"And she leaves... and becomes"
The פסוק compares becoming married to leaving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers ריש לקיש's question from step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A שטר אירוסין must be written לשמה, because the פסוק compares becoming married to leaving a marriage.

steps.title: Applying ריש לקיש to the three opinions
steps.stepSummary: In the ברייתא, one opinion follows ריש לקיש and the other does not. So the argument is about לשמה, not about loans.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds like ריש לקיש, and the other master does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how this explanation fits the ברייתא. The opinions split over whether ריש לקיש's rule is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says she is not betrothed, because he follows ריש לקיש and the שטר was not written for her. רבי אלעזר says she is betrothed, because he does not follow ריש לקיש. חכמים are unsure, so they again count only the paper's money value. Either way, the ברייתא is not about betrothing with a loan.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds of / he does not hold of

steps.whatToRemember: In this explanation, the ברייתא is about whether a שטר אירוסין must be written לשמה, not about betrothing with a loan.

phrases.english: One master holds like ריש לקיש,
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר, who says she is not betrothed.

phrases.english: and the other master does not hold like ריש לקיש.
phrases.notes: This is רבי אלעזר, who says she is betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It connects ריש לקיש's answer back to the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It finishes pushing off the proof from step 8.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument in the ברייתא is about ריש לקיש's rule, not about betrothing with a loan.

steps.title: A third explanation: written for her but without her knowledge
steps.stepSummary: Everyone accepts ריש לקיש. The ברייתא is about a שטר written for her but without her knowledge, which is the same argument that later אמוראים have.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, everyone holds like ריש לקיש. Here the case is one where he wrote it for her sake but without her knowledge. They argue about the same point that רבא and רבינא argue about with רב פפא and רב שרביא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third way to read the ברייתא. This one does not need anyone to reject ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שטר was written for her, so ריש לקיש's rule is met. The open question is whether it also has to be written with her knowledge. Again, the ברייתא is not about betrothing with a loan.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with?

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: everyone holds like ריש לקיש,
and here, what case are we dealing with?
Where he wrote it for her sake but without her knowledge.
And they disagree about the dispute of רבא and רבינא
with רב פפא and רב שרביא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is another way to explain the ברייתא, so the תנאים do not have to argue about ריש לקיש.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It again rejects reading the ברייתא as being about a loan.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be about a שטר written for her but without her knowledge.

steps.title: The אמוראים argue about a document written without her knowledge
steps.stepSummary: רבא and רבינא say she is betrothed. רב פפא and רב שרביא say she is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: if he wrote it for her sake but without her knowledge, רבא and רבינא say she is betrothed. רב פפא and רב שרביא say she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the argument between the אמוראים that step 15 pointed to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the שטר was written for her. They argue only about whether her knowing about it at the time of writing is also needed. The same split could explain the opinions in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: As it was stated:
If he wrote it for her sake but without her knowledge,
רבא and רבינא say: she is betrothed;

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב שֵׁרֵבְיָא אָמְרִי: אֵינָהּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת.
phrases.english: רב פפא and רב שרביא say: she is not betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It gives the source for the dispute that step 15 mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שטר written for her but without her knowledge: רבא and רבינא say she is betrothed, and רב פפא and רב שרביא say she is not.

steps.title: New attempt: the case of the jewelry and betrothing with a debt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again suggests that betrothing with a loan is a dispute between תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא about a woman who asks a craftsman to make her jewelry and says she will be betrothed to him in return.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is a dispute between these תנאים. As it was taught: if she said, "Make me bracelets, earrings and rings, and I will be betrothed to you," once he makes them she is betrothed. This is the opinion of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say she is not betrothed until money reaches her hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a fresh try at the same question from step 7. It brings a new ברייתא in which רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once he finishes the jewelry, she owes him payment for his work. So when רבי מאיר says she is betrothed, it looks like she is betrothed with a debt. The חכמים require something new to actually reach her hand.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it is like these תנאים (that they argue about this)

steps.confusionAlert: She is the one who asked for the work, so she owes him for it. That debt is what links this case to betrothing with a loan.

phrases.english: Let us say it is like these תנאים,
as it was taught in a ברייתא:
"Make me bracelets, earrings and rings,
and I will be betrothed to you":
once he has made them, she is betrothed;
these are the words of רבי מאיר.
And the חכמים say: she is not betrothed
until money reaches her hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first proof was pushed off, so the גמרא returns to the question from step 7 with a new ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That betrothing with a loan is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the jewelry, where רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue.

steps.title: Which money do the Sages mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'money' the חכמים require. It shows that it cannot mean the jewelry itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this 'money'? If you say it is the jewelry itself, that would mean the first opinion does not require even the jewelry. But then with what would she be betrothed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the חכמים mean by 'money' in the jewelry ברייתא. It rules out the first possible answer, which is the jewelry itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'money' meant the jewelry, then תנא קמא, who argues with the חכמים, would hold that she is betrothed without even getting the jewelry. That makes no sense, because the jewelry is the only thing he gives her. So 'money' must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: what are the circumstances? What case is this?
by inference, it would follow that
the first opinion in the ברייתא (here רבי מאיר)

steps.confusionAlert: 'That very money' means the jewelry she asked for. It does not mean coins. The jewelry is the object he hands her.

phrases.english: This 'money': what are its circumstances?
phrases.notes: He means the חכמים' words in the ברייתא: she is not betrothed until money reaches her hand.

phrases.english: If we say it means that very money,
it follows that the first opinion holds:
even that very money is also not needed!
But then with what is she betrothed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out the meaning of the ברייתא quoted in step 17, to build the proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What 'money' the חכמים require before she is betrothed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not the jewelry itself, because then תנא קמא's view would make no sense.

steps.title: The חכמים require other money, so this is a dispute about a loan
steps.stepSummary: The 'money' the חכמים require must be other money, given to her beyond his letting go of the wage she owes. So רבי מאיר holds that letting go of that debt betroths her, and the ברייתא is a dispute about מקדש במלוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must mean other money, and so we learn that they argue about betrothing with a loan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the חכמים require 'other money,' meaning something beyond the wage she owes the craftsman. So the ברייתא shows an argument about betrothing with a loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He tries to betroth her by letting go of the payment she owes him for making the jewelry. A debt she owes is like a loan. So רבי מאיר says that works, and the חכמים say she needs real money in hand.

keyTerms.meaning: other money, meaning something given to her beyond letting go of the wage she owes

phrases.english: Rather, is it not about other money,
phrases.notes: The חכמים want something new handed to her. Letting go of the payment she owes for his work is not enough.

phrases.english: and learn from this
that they disagree about one who betroths with a loan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו בְּמָמוֹן אַחֵר, וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the jewelry ruled out, the only option left is the wage, which completes the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That מקדש במלוה is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The jewelry ברייתא, with 'money' read as the wage she owes.

steps.title: The assumption behind the proof: wages build up as he works
steps.stepSummary: The proof assumes that everyone agrees the wage is owed from the start of the work. So by the end, it is a loan. Then the dispute must be about loans.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they must assume everyone agrees a wage builds up from beginning to end, so it is a loan. So isn't the argument this: one Sage says betrothing with a loan works, and one says it does not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the hidden assumption that the proof needs. Then it restates the proof clearly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wage only counts as a loan if she already owed it while he was working. That is the idea of יֶשְׁנָהּ לִשְׂכִירוּת מִתְּחִלָּה וְעַד סוֹף. If everyone accepts that, then the only thing left to argue about is whether a loan can betroth.

keyTerms.meaning: the wage is owed bit by bit from the beginning of the work to the end
is it not that...? (introduces a suggested proof)

steps.confusionAlert: יֶשְׁנָהּ לִשְׂכִירוּת מִתְּחִלָּה וְעַד סוֹף does not mean he gets paid as he goes. It means her debt to him keeps growing while he works. So when he finishes, she already owes him.

phrases.english: And they assume that everyone agrees
a wage is owed from the beginning to the end
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording, so read it as 'from beginning to end.'

phrases.english: and so it is a loan.
Is it not about this that they disagree,
that one Sage holds:
one who betroths with a loan, she is betrothed,
and the other Sage holds:
one who betroths with a loan, she is not betrothed?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבְרִי דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא יֶשְׁנָהּ לִשְׂכִירוּת מִתְּחִלָּה וְעַד סוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows which assumption step 19 depends on, and states the proof in full.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר holds a loan can betroth and the חכמים hold it cannot.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The jewelry ברייתא, read with the assumption that the wage builds up from the start.

steps.title: No, the argument is about when the wage becomes owed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Everyone agrees a loan cannot betroth. The real argument is whether a wage builds up from beginning to end.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees betrothing with a loan does not work. Here they argue about whether a wage is owed from beginning to end. One Sage holds:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. It moves the argument away from loans and onto the question of when a wage is owed. It begins to explain each side, and the explanation continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on everyone agreeing that the wage builds up as he works. The גמרא now says that point itself is the argument. So the ברייתא no longer proves anything about loans. Everyone can agree that a loan cannot betroth.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא. It takes the hidden assumption a proof relies on and says that is the real point of the argument.

phrases.english: No, everyone agrees
one who betroths with a loan, she is not betrothed,
and here, about whether a wage is owed
from the beginning to the end, they disagree.
One Sage holds:

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מְקַדֵּשׁ בְּמִלְוָה אֵינָהּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from steps 19-20 by questioning the shared assumption it relied on.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof that the jewelry ברייתא shows a dispute about מקדש במלוה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed everyone agrees a wage builds up from beginning to end. That is really what they argue about.
